title: Clair Patterson
summary: American geochemist Clair Patterson (1922–1995) developed uranium-lead isotopic dating methods to calculate the age of the Earth at 4.55 billion years in 1953 using the Canyon Diablo meteorite. Realizing that ubiquitous environmental lead compromised his ultra-clean laboratory measurements, Patterson subsequently uncovered widespread industrial lead contamination in the biosphere, oceans, and polar ice caps, leading a decades-long campaign that spurred the elimination of leaded gasoline and food can solders to protect public health.

uncertainty.note: Born 2 June 1922 in Mitchellville, Iowa; died 5 December 1995 in Sea Ranch, California.

where.modern_name: California Institute of Technology (Caltech), Pasadena, California, United States (working base where Patterson built cleanrooms, dated the Earth, and measured global lead pollution from 1952 until 1995)

importance.justification: Patterson established the accurate age of the Earth and almost single-handedly exposed and fought global industrial lead poisoning.

related.because: Patterson's lead-isotope measurements on the Canyon Diablo meteorite provided the first accurate calculation of the age of the Earth.

sources.title: Immeasurable: The impact of geochemist Clair C. Patterson, PhD'51, who determined the age of the earth and fought lead pollution
sources.author: Jason Kelly

reviewer_note: Pinned to Caltech in Pasadena where Patterson spent his academic career from 1952 to 1995, built the first geochemical cleanroom, and did his seminal dating and lead-pollution work.
